newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-Irrespondible to play Mehrtens - Smith.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-Irrespondible to play Mehrtens - Smith.

text.p: Canterbury Crusaders would not be irresponsible and play All Black Andrew Mehrtens in a Super 12 rugby match against ACT Brumbies at Canberra on Saturday, coach Wayne Smith said on Thursday.
Mehrtens tore his hamstring in a warm-up game against ACT in Greymouth on February 21 and has not recovered sufficiently to play on Saturday.
Smith said it was disappointing that Mehrtens was not fully fit yet because he had the potential to play a major part in the Crusaders' game plan.
Without the All Black, Canterbury have had a win and a loss, after finishing bottom of the table last year.
"We knew last month it would take three to five weeks before he would be right," Smith said.
"We were hoping he would return to full fitness more quickly, but if he was to play on Saturday and then tear his hamstring again, it would be irresponsible on out part."

Mehrtens will play his first Super 12 game against Waikato Chiefs in Timaru on Easter Saturday, after missing all of last year's series because of a serious knee injury sustained on the All Blacks' tour of Italy and France in 1995.
Leon MacDonald, the Marlborough teenager, will have his third game at first five-eighth while lock Norm Maxwell is expected to run out for the first time, possibly as a replacement, against ACT.
Smith has not yet named his playing 15 because of a number of injuries to players.

Drafted Aucklander Waisake Sotutu will not make the trip to Canberra but will play a Christchurch senior club game for University, to help build up his match speed and confidence. Sotutu, who has not played a Super 12 match this season, is recovering from a knee injury.

Sotutu will return to play next week against the Chiefs, who will be without their suspended prop Richard Loe. He has lost the chance to play against his old Crusader team-mates after being found guilty of punching in the Auckland Blues game last weekend.

The Crusaders are still looking for a loose forward replacement for hooker John Akurangi, who has a broken arm, while Canterbury Colt Reuben Thorne has been added to the squad as temporary No 8 cover for injured Steve Surridge.
Crusaders squad to travel to Canberra:

Daryl Lilley, James Kerr, Paula Bale, Daryl Gibson, Tabai Matson, Mark Mayerhofler, Leon MacDonald, Justin Marshall, Aaron Flynn, Clarke McLeod, Scott Robertson, Angus Gardiner, Todd Blackadder (captain), Steve Lancaster, Mark Weedon, Norm Maxwell, Con Barrell, Stu Loe, Kevin Nepia, Mark Hammett, Matt Sexton.
